# Source doc-test port

All 109 fenced blocks in the five pinned 1.99.0 files were extracted. 80 Rust examples run as separate tests against the copy: 55 from ip_addr.rs, 24 from socket_addr.rs, and one from parser.rs. mod.rs and display_buffer.rs contain no code fences. Only std::net:: and core::net:: import paths change. Assertions and input literals remain verbatim. The test wrapper supplies the implicit main body used by rustdoc. Hidden `# ` lines are included; `##` lines become literal `#` lines. This snapshot has no hidden lines.

The 24 examples with feature attributes cannot be ported under the stable, import-only rules. Their complete code is retained in [doc-tests.json](doc-tests.json). Six require addr_parse_ascii, three require ip_as_octets, and 15 require ip. No feature line is removed. Their stable compiler failures are recorded in evidence/gen/doc-unported-*.txt. These exclusions limit the meaning of the full upstream suite in this study. Four text/no_rust diagrams are not Rust tests. The should_panic example is skipped as requested; it would normally be a panic-expecting rustdoc test. No ignore or compile_fail block occurs in this snapshot.

[DOC-TEST-REWRITES.patch](DOC-TEST-REWRITES.patch) records every import rewrite, including excluded blocks. [doc-tests.json](doc-tests.json) records original code, runnable code, source ranges, tags and disposition for every block. Extraction is replayed by run_all.sh before testing.
